section_1.title: Intuition: Transformations as Geometric Movement
section_1.content: Define a linear transformation as a function that maps vectors to vectors, preserving grid lines (parallel remains parallel) and keeping the origin fixed.
section_1.example: Imagine a digital 'Cat' character on a 2D plane. A transformation stretches, rotates, or shears the cat while ensuring its whiskers (vectors) remain connected to the origin.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Basis Vectors
section_2.content: Explain that any 2D vector [x, y] is just a combination of basis vectors i-hat [1, 0] and j-hat [0, 1]. The transformation is defined entirely by where these two vectors land.
section_2.example: Visualize a grid with two unit arrows. When we 'transform' the space, we track only where these two specific arrows point after the move.

section_3.title: The Matrix: Encoding the Transformation
section_3.content: Introduce the matrix as a concise container. The columns of the matrix represent the new coordinates of i-hat and j-hat. Matrix-vector multiplication is simply applying this change to any input vector.
section_3.example: If i-hat moves to [1, 2] and j-hat moves to [-1, 1], the matrix is [[1, -1], [2, 1]]. Multiply this by a vector [3, 2] to see where the 'Cat''s foot lands.

section_4.title: Synthesis: Application in Computer Graphics
section_4.content: Summarize how matrices allow us to perform complex operations (rotations/scaling) by simple multiplication, forming the backbone of video game engines and animation.
section_4.example: Show a 2D robot character spinning: each frame is just the robot's current position matrix multiplied by a 'rotation' matrix.

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Map to right side of screen
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Intuition: Transformations as Geometric Movement", 
                          ["Transformations map vectors to new vectors.", 
                           "Grid lines must remain parallel.", 
                           "The origin always stays fixed."])
        
        # Setup coordinate plane

        self.place_in_area(plane, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.add(plane)
        
        vector = Vector([1, 1], color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(vector, 'D3', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(vector))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        self.play(
            plane.animate.apply_matrix(matrix),
            vector.animate.apply_matrix(matrix),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED)
        self.wait(1)

    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Basis Vectors", [
            "Any 2D vector is a basis combination.",
            "Basis vectors are i-hat and j-hat.",
            "Transformations depend on basis vector movement."
        ])
        
        # Define base vectors
        i_hat = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT, color="#FF0000", buff=0)
        j_hat = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP, color="#00FF00", buff=0)

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
